title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a working sheet from the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes. The neighbouring pages are pieces of an unrelated typescript (an English translation of a textbook on algebraic varieties) used as scrap paper, so they give no mathematical context. The page has two parts.

(1) Top half. Here G is a motivic Galois group (the Tannakian group of a subcategory of motives) and i: Gm_C -> G_C is a cocharacter attached to a realization, presumably a Hodge-type or weight-type cocharacter. Some 'special circumstance' (it follows a crossed-out remark about 'positivity structure' and 'analogy') lets Grothendieck pick privileged polarizations (or structures) on the G_i, compatible with the cocharacter i.
- He asks how arbitrary this choice is. Writing i - i' presupposes that G (or G°) is commutative.
- He notes that the differences i - i' range over (or lie in) a subgroup of finite index of Hom(Gm_C, G°_C). He adds that this says nothing about how the corresponding i_0 - i_0' behave, and judges the question secondary.
- Conclusion: one gets privileged ('R-'?) fibre functors, defined in terms of the various i. 'R' may mean real-valued fibre functors, which would fit with the positivity and polarization theme.

(2) Bottom half: 'other specific structures on the G coming from a finite field'.
- For motives over F_q, G_C = D_C(M) is a diagonalizable group (a torus up to a finite group). Its character group M is a subgroup of L*, generated by the Frobenius eigenvalues (Weil q-numbers) in a number field L.
- L is CM or totally real, so complex conjugation is central in Gal(L/Q), commutes with the Galois action, and acts on M by pi -> pi-bar = q^w/pi.
- Hence G carries a canonical involution u -> u'. Its effect on a distinguished (weight?) element appears to be the identity, which 'practically suffices to determine it'.
- On the cocharacter group Hom(Gm_C, G_C) = Hom(M, Z), the involution induces complex conjugation.

In modern terms, this is the Weil-number (pro)torus P of the conjectural category of motives over F_q (Tate conjecture plus semisimplicity), together with its complex-conjugation involution. The related ideas of polarizations and positivity, and of lifting to characteristic 0 via cocharacters, feed later into Saavedra/Deligne–Milne polarizations and the Langlands–Rapoport/Milne description of motives over finite fields.
errors: Writing i - i' only makes sense if G° (or G) is commutative. That holds for motives over F_q or CM-type motives, but it is not stated on this part of the page.
The finite-index claim about the set of differences i - i' is asserted without justification. The page itself says the information obtained is incomplete.
L need not be CM: for an odd power of p, sqrt(q) generates a real field. Complex conjugation is still central in Gal(L/Q) (trivial in that case), so the construction survives.

ideas.what: The motivic Galois group of motives over a finite field is diagonalizable, G = D(M), with M a subgroup of L* generated by Weil q-numbers.
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number protorus P of motives over F_q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck circle; Saavedra Rivano (1972), Langlands–Rapoport (1987), Milne ('Motives over finite fields', 1994)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own published texts as far as I know; appears in Saavedra's Catégories tannakiennes (his student) and in Milne

ideas.what: A canonical involution on G induced by complex conjugation on the CM field of Weil numbers (pi -> q^w/pi); on cocharacters it is complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation / Rosati-type involution on the Weil-number torus

ideas.what: Privileged polarizations tied to cocharacters i: Gm_C -> G_C, with the arbitrariness of i measured by a finite-index subgroup of the cocharacter group.
ideas.modern_name: Hodge/weight cocharacters and polarizations of Tannakian categories

ideas.what: Privileged (possibly real) fibre functors defined in terms of the cocharacters i.
ideas.modern_name: Fibre functors and torsors in Tannakian categories; real fibre functors and polarizations

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks how arbitrary the choice of cocharacter i (and so of privileged polarizations or fibre functors) is. He gets a finite-index subgroup of cocharacters, leaves the behaviour of i_0 - i_0' open and calls it secondary. This is close to later questions on how unique the 'Hodge cocharacter' attached to CM liftings of motives over F_q is (Langlands–Rapoport, Milne).
missed.quote: Quel est l'arbitraire ? ... mais cela ne donne aucune indication ... Question semble secondaire.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It shows the Weil-number torus, its involution and its cocharacter or polarization data being considered in Grothendieck's own notes, earlier than the usual credits. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches the Weil-number torus of motives over F_q with its complex-conjugation involution, plus polarization and cocharacter considerations. These are known (Saavedra, Langlands–Rapoport, Milne) but are rarely credited directly to Grothendieck's own manuscripts. The page is historically notable but not mathematically new, and the date (1965 vs. c. 1977) is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: 'R-factorisations [?] fibres privilégiés' should read 'R-foncteurs fibres privilégiés' (R possibly real-valued).
'définis au tenseur [?] des différents i' is more likely 'définis en termes des différents i'.
'd'après le fait [?] de' is likely 'd'après la forme de'.
'Ca une involution canonique, notée' should read 'Ça [définit] une involution canonique, notée u ↦ u'', with the 'u ↦ u'' written above the line.
'Dans [-l'algèbre-]': the crossed-out word is uncertain, and the bottom line probably concerns the image of the weight/regular element being fixed ('c'est l'identité'). Reading uncertain.
'qui commute [?] [?] Gal(L/Q)' should read 'qui commute à Gal(L/Q)'.
In the top line, the struck-out text reads approximately 'Question de structure de positivité et de ... analogie ... i liés'.
'Hom(Gm_C, G°_C)' is correct, with G° the identity component.
